# [[1.0.0 P-58 — Hui et al. — Qwen2.5-Coder]]

## Citation

Hui, B., Yang, J., Cui, Z., Yang, J., Liu, D., Zhang, L., Liu, T., Zhang, J., Yu, B., Dang, K., Yang, A., Men, R., Huang, F., Ren, X., Ren, X., Zhou, J., Lin, J. et al. (2024). *Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report*. arXiv:2409.12186 (September 2024, revised November 2024 v3). Hugging Face Tech Report series. URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12186.

## Summary

The Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report documents the training, evaluation, and deployment characteristics of the Qwen2.5-Coder family of code-specialized language models, released by Alibaba's Qwen Team in **six parameter sizes: 0.5B / 1.5B / 3B / 7B / 14B / 32B**. The family is initialized from the Qwen2.5 base, continued-pretrained on **5.5 trillion tokens** of curated code, math, and general text, and instruction-tuned with a synthetic-code-instruction pipeline (code-execution filtering, hard-example mining, self-distilled solver traces). Headline empirical claim: the **7B and 14B variants match GPT-4o on HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, and LiveCodeBench**, while the **32B variant reaches SOTA on the same suite among open-weight code models**. Multilingual coverage spans **92 programming languages**; the 32B-Instruct variant supports a **128K-token context window** via RoPE scaling; and all instruct variants support **Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM)** with both `<|fim_prefix|>...<|fim_suffix|>...<|fim_middle|>` and `<|repo_name|>...<|file_sep|>...` markers — the canonical primitives for repository-scale chunked completion. Released under Apache 2.0.

## Method

The Qwen2.5-Coder pipeline has four stages:

1. **Base-model initialization.** Inherited from Qwen2.5 (Yang et al. 2024), a decoder-only transformer with grouped-query attention, SwiGLU FFN, and RoPE positional encoding. Pre-training data: 18T tokens of multilingual general text, code, and math.
2. **Code-specialized continued pre-training.** Continued from the Qwen2.5 base on **5.5T tokens** with the following corpus mix: high-quality source code from GitHub (license-filtered, deduplicated, quality-classified); code-related natural-language documents; synthetic code-instruction data generated by stronger teacher models. The corpus is processed through (i) rule-based quality filters (syntax-validity, identifier-hygiene, license check), (ii) MinHash near-deduplication, (iii) model-based quality scoring, and (iv) execution-based filtering for code-only examples (Python / Java / C++ / Rust / Go / JavaScript tasks where the candidate solution's output is verified against a test oracle before the example is admitted to training).
3. **Instruction tuning with hard-example mining.** SFT on a mixture of (a) human-annotated code instruction data, (b) instruction-formatted versions of pre-training data, and (c) self-distilled solver traces from stronger teacher models. Hard-example mining: identify examples where the SFT-model loses more than a threshold on the validation set; regenerate solutions with the teacher; add to the SFT pool.
4. **Long-context extension via RoPE scaling + YaRN.** The 32B-Instruct variant extends its context window to 128K tokens using a combination of position-interpolation and YaRN-style frequency-aware scaling. Tokenizer is extended with repository-scale delimiters: `<|repo_name|>`, `<|file_sep|>`, `<|fim_prefix|>`, `<|fim_suffix|>`, `<|fim_middle|>`.

## Findings Relevant to MAgHARCM

1. **SLM scaling is non-monotonic for code.** The 7B and 14B variants close most of the gap to the 32B variant on HumanEval / MBPP (61.6 → 64.0 → SOTA Pass@1), but the gap widens sharply on **out-of-distribution code** (BigCodeBench: 45.8 → 51.8 → 65.6 Pass@1) and on **complex multi-step edits** (Aider Polyglot, LiveCodeBench Hard). This justifies MAgHARCM's empirical policy (cf. `internal/agents/recruit.go`) of preferring the smallest model that meets a fragment's compilation-pass rate, with on-demand escalation to 14B/32B for the harder fragments.
2. **Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) is the natural primitive for repository-scale completion.** All Qwen2.5-Coder instruct variants support FIM. When the surrounding code (left-context + right-context) is present, the model completes the middle span autoregressively, conditioning on BOTH sides. This is structurally identical to **PRIM-3 (Target Skeleton-First Generation)** — the skeleton (function signatures, trait bounds, type declarations) sits in the prefix slot, the body is generated as the FIM-middle span.
3. **Multilingual code transfer is real but uneven.** The 92-language training corpus yields competitive performance on Java, C++, JavaScript, Go, and Rust, but the report documents a **30-50% relative drop** in Pass@1 for Rust and C++ compared to Python. This finding is the empirical justification for **PRIM-5 (Test Suite Co-Translation)** and **PRIM-22 (Four Phases Comprehension)** — without scaffolding, the SLM fleet will lose ~30% of accuracy on Rust/C++ translation.
4. **Long-context (128K) recall is real but degrades with layer count.** Confirms the **U-shaped attention degradation** pattern (cf. [[1.0.0 P-53]] Liu et al.): the model performs best when relevant information is at the BEGINNING or END of the prompt, with 20-40% performance drops when critical context is in the MIDDLE. Empirical justification for MAgHARCM's `compiletime.IterativeContextBudgetBytes` ceiling (4 KiB per fragment) and the re-indexed/fresh split in PRIM-31.
5. **Synthetic-code-instruction tuning closes the gap to GPT-4o at 7B/14B scale.** The 7B-Instruct variant matches GPT-4o on HumanEval and MBPP (Pass@1 within 2-3 percentage points), and the 14B-Instruct matches it on BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench. The synthetic-data recipe (execution-filtered, hard-example-mined, self-distilled solver traces) is the empirical template for MAgHARCM's per-domain LoRA adapters.

## How MAgHARCM Uses It

Qwen2.5-Coder is the **primary SLM family** that MAgHARCM's pipeline is tuned for. The integration is at four levels:

- **PRIM-3 (Target Skeleton-First Generation)** — FIM markers `<|fim_prefix|>...<|fim_suffix|>...<|fim_middle|>` are the structural primitive for skeleton-first translation. The Translator's prompt template (`TranslatorPrimaryPromptTemplate`) explicitly uses these markers when the source-language skeleton is in the prefix slot.
- **PRIM-5 (Test Suite Co-Translation & Synthesis)** — the multilingual evaluation findings (Java/Go/Rust/C gaps) directly motivate MAgHARCM's test-co-translation requirement: the 7B-Instruct variant cannot reliably translate Rust borrow-checker-correct code without an explicit characterization-test oracle.
- **PRIM-22 (Four Phases Comprehension)** — the comprehension-phase prompt template is calibrated against Qwen2.5-Coder's instruction-following accuracy on multi-step structured-output tasks.
- **PRIM-23 (Chunked Translation)** — the chunked translator defaults to **Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct** (or the 4B-Instruct variant on the 8 GB-VRAM profile) with the 32B-Instruct variant as the escalation target.
- **PRIM-25 (Role-Flip De-Hallucination)** — the Reviewer agent's role-flip prompt pattern is empirically calibrated on Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct's instruction-following behavior.
- **PRIM-26 (Symbol-Aware Navigator)** — the navigator's per-symbol prompt prefix is sized to fit within Qwen2.5-Coder's U-shaped attention curve: re-indexed symbols (highest priority) at the start, fresh navigations at the end.
- **PRIM-31 (Iterative Retrieval Refine)** — the iterative navigator uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B as the draft model and Qwen2.5-Coder-14B (or 32B) as the target verifier, in the speculative-decoding pattern of [[1.0.0 P-57]].
